The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
President Trump made his closing arguments
for the midterm elections at the reflecting pool in Washington, D.C. today,
but first drew attention to the expensive,
problem-plagued repair job of the pool
and his attempts to crack down on crime in the city.
"We went through a lot with vandalism.
The vandalism was unprecedented.
People don't like talking about it."
D.C. residents can't elect a voting member of Congress.
After 20 minutes devoted to D.C. construction projects,
Trump said tomorrow's elections are the most important midterms in our lifetime.
"We've achieved more in less than two years
than any administration in American history,
and I've kept every single promise I made except far more.
I've actually kept far more promises than I made.
We've done much more than I promised."
Trump accused Democrats of nominating,
quote, "the most extreme and dangerous slate of candidates in American history."
House Republicans will hold their leadership elections next week.
NPR's Claudia Grisales reports Speaker Mike Johnson
says he intends to remain the House Republican leader regardless of the election results.
Speaker Johnson is pushed back on projections that House Republicans
could lose control of the lower chamber to Democrats.
However, he told CBS last month he believes he'll remain leader
regardless of the outcome from these elections.
"I would expect my colleagues would ask me to continue leading this conference,
even if we have divided government."
Last month, Johnson reached three years in the post.
He took the House gavel after a tumultuous period for the House GOP conference
that saw former Speaker Kevin McCarthy ousted.
House Republicans are on track to hold internal elections
for several leadership positions, including Johnson's on Nov. 10.
The full House will vote for Speaker on Jan. 3, 2027.
Claudia Grisales, NPR News.
The FDA has approved the first generic version of a twice-yearly injection that prevents HIV,
and NPR's Jonathan Lambert reports the move could help make the medicine more affordable
in lower-income countries.
In June 2025, an HIV drug hailed as the "breakthrough of the year" was approved by the FDA.
The drug, called Lenacapavir, is the closest tool to a vaccine that's available.
Just two shots a year is 99 percent effective at preventing HIV infection.
But it's expensive.
In the U.S., it costs about $28,000 a year.
To make it cheaper, drugmaker Gilead Sciences negotiated generic licensing agreements
with several manufacturers.
The Indian company Dr. Reddy's Laboratories is the first to get FDA approval.
Their generic version is expected to cost roughly $40 a year,
which could drastically expand the drug's reach.
Under the agreement, it will be available in 120 lower-income countries,
and the company says doses could start shipping next month.
Jonathan Lambert, NPR News.
Major U.S. stock indexes finished mixed today, the S&P 500 fell more than half a percent,
even though the majority of stocks within the index climbed.
This is NPR.
The Kennedy Center has announced that Paul Anka, David Foster, Andy Garcia, David Mamet,
and Barbara Mandrell will be honored at this year's Kennedy Center Honors.
The event will take place away from the iconic venue for the first time
due to President Trump's legal battle over renovations and naming rights.
A Republican senator is speaking out against the Trump administration's
proposal for unprecedented changes to the next census.
The plan would reshape voting maps and how federal funding is distributed across the country,
NPR's Hansi Lo Wang reports.
Republican Senator Lisa Murkowski of Alaska joined two dozen Senate Democrats,
plus independent Senator Angus King of Maine,
in urging the Trump administration to withdraw its proposal for the 2030 census.
It calls for excluding millions of people living in the states without U.S. citizenship
or green card from a key census count that, according to the 14th amendment,
must include the "whole number of persons" in each state.
That count is used to determine each state's share of congressional seats
and Electoral College votes for a decade.
Murkowski and the other senators say the administration's proposal
"violates the clear meaning of the Constitution."
Trump officials also propose cutting questions about race and ethnicity
because they see a "reduced need" for that information,
which is used for enforcing civil and voting rights laws.
Hansi Lo Wang, NPR News A new dinosaur dig site near Arches
National Park in Utah could be one of the oldest Cretaceous bone beds in North America.
According to KSL News, fossils found at the site outside of Moab could date back 138 to 141
million years. They also believe the site could contain a new dinosaur species.
Scientists hope the discovery will help them better understand a mass
extinction event that happened during the transition between the Jurassic.
